transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-05
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE); Dr. Sora Tanaka (CTO, Kyoto Biosystems); Miguel Alvarez (Head of Security); Priya Singh (Product)

Summary (auto):
- Quick posture readout and gap scan for SOC 2 / ISO27001 alignment.
- Trust Center admin workflow and evidence hand-off discussed.
- KMS integration options (Redwood-managed vs customer KMS) and data residency concerns (JP/US) flagged.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, and with me is liam our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Sora: good thanks, thanks for making time. we wanted to go through our SOC2/ISO posture and specifically understand how we can onboard audit teams to the trust center.
[00:12] Miguel: yeah and also, timeline — we have a regulatory audit for a partner contract end of Q3. so we need to map controls and identify gaps.
[00:18] Maya: got it. high level first — do you already have a SOC 2 type II report? or are you partway through?
[00:23] Priya: we have a type II for infra components from last year, but it doesn't fully cover our new inference platform and some third-party integrations.
[00:31] Miguel: also we need iso27001 scoping, some controls are shared, so we want to avoid duplicate work.
[00:35] Liam: okay makes sense. i'll try to call out where redwood's trust center artifacts map to common soc/iso controls. quick note — sometimes the transcript here will show product names a little off, like 'redwood consol' instead of 'redwood console' or 'k-v cash', so please ignore that if it shows up.
[00:46] Sora: ha, yes. no problem.
[00:48] Maya: first practical bit — we can share a redacted SOC 2 Type II into the trust center. we usually provide a redwood-managed report but we can also give limited access for customers to upload their own artifacts.
[00:57] Miguel: ideally we want to give our auditors read-only access, with RBAC limiting what they can see — not all teams should access customer PII or production logs. can redwood do per-role scoping?
[01:06] Liam: yes. Trust Center has role-based access — we have Administrator, Auditor, and Viewer roles. Admins can manage invites, Auditors can view evidence and reports but cannot change storage settings, Viewers are very limited. there's also an 'evidence-only' role we often spin up for external firms.
[01:20] Priya: who manages invites? our preference is Kyoto handles invites for internal auditors, but external auditor invites should be short-lived.
[01:27] Maya: you can manage invites from your console; we can also coordinate initially. we'll need an NDA uploaded before external invites in most cases — that's our standard.
[01:33] Miguel: fine. what about SSO? we use SAML and Okta.
[01:37] Liam: we support SSO via SAML and OIDC. Okta is a common one, and the flow is straightforward — we provide a metadata endpoint and an SP configuration. sometimes the attribute mapping needs manual tweaks for group membership to match RBAC in the Trust Center.
[01:50] Sora: and how long to get SSO configured?
[01:52] Liam: initial SSO can be done in a day if you have an Okta admin ready; full group mapping and end-to-end test, maybe 2-3 days depending on your internal sign-offs.
[01:58] Maya: right, we typically recommend enabling SSO before granting auditor roles so everything is tied to your identity provider.
[02:05] Miguel: good. lets talk about encryption — we keep all customer data encrypted at rest, but our compliance folks need to know whether keys are customer-managed or Redwood-managed.
[02:13] Liam: we support both. options: Redwood-managed KMS (we handle rotation and HSM-backed storage internally), or customer-managed keys via external KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). for high assurance you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with HSM integration. note: some customers call our path "Redwood KMS" or the 'hosted KMS' in docs.
[02:31] Priya: if we choose customer KMS, do we still see audit logs in our region? our product team insists logs are retained in JP.
[02:36] Liam: yes — you can pick a region for data residency. logs and artifacts stored within the trust center will be placed in the region you select (we support us-east, eu-west, ap-northeast-1 for JP). when you configure a customer KMS, keys remain in your cloud tenancy; redwood never stores the plaintext keys.
[02:52] Miguel: retention — our policy is 7 years for certain control evidence. can trust center handle long-retention archives?
[02:58] Maya: yes, evidence can be tiered to cold storage with lifecycle rules; retention windows are configurable and we can support long retention, but there are cost implications. we can provide an estimate for 7-year retention in the follow-up.
[03:10] Sora: is there support for transfer logs or chain-of-custody? we have to show auditors how evidence moved from product team to the trust center.
[03:17] Liam: we store immutable audit trails for uploads, downloads, and permission changes. every artifact has a metadata timeline — who uploaded, which commit or ticket it came from (if linked), and any transformation. it's part of our audit log function. there is also an API to stream logs into your SIEM.
[03:29] Miguel: which SIEMs are supported?
[03:31] Liam: we have built connectors for Splunk and SumoLogic, generic syslog/CloudWatch ingestion and an S3 export for longterm archives. you can also stream via Kafka if you want.
[03:39] Priya: ok great.
[03:40] Maya: quick question on scope — do you want us to map Redwood controls to your ISO27001 annex A control ids, or do you want a SOC2-to-ISO crosswalk?
[03:48] Sora: both, ideally. the iso audit team wants an annex A mapping but our legal team prefers seeing the SOC controls that map to contractual obligations.
[03:55] Miguel: yes, can you provide both? even if it's a high-level crosswalk first.
[03:59] Liam: we have a standard controls matrix that maps our platform artifacts to SOC 2 CC criteria and ISO27001 annex A. i can share a template. note that for some operational controls you'll need to provide customer-specific evidence (for example, your deployment change management artifacts).
[04:12] Maya: we'll upload the matrix to the trust center and tag which artifacts we can pre-populate.
[04:17] Sora: about evidence — what format do you accept? we have PDFs, screenshots, system exports.
[04:22] Liam: most common formats are PDFs and CSVs; we also accept JSON archives and links to cloud storage. for automation we recommend using the API to push artifacts; otherwise manual upload works for ad-hoc items.
[04:32] Miguel: is there a way to link artifacts to tickets in JIRA? that would help for change control evidence.
[04:36] Liam: yes, the metadata supports external references — ticket id, commit sha, PR link. you can include those during upload or via API enrichment.
[04:45] Priya: we have a product question — there is some confusion internally about the 'dedicated' option vs the hosted trust center. if we go dedicated for inference, does that affect how trust center data is surfaced?
[04:55] Maya: good call-out. if you have a Dedicated deployment, a lot of telemetry is still surfaced to the Trust Center, but there are deployment knobs. with private or on-prem you can opt for a private trust center endpoint inside your VPC — effectively Trust Center data remains inside your network and you maintain the control plane.
[05:12] Sora: we are leaning towards a hybrid: hosted control plane but dedicated inference nodes in our VPC. would that be a problem for evidence collection?
[05:20] Liam: not a problem — we can collect evidence agents from the VPC and push to the trust center endpoint over the customer-controlled network path; the metadata and audit logs will show source IPs and the nodes involved.
[05:29] Miguel: one more on encryption — rotation policy. auditors love to see rotation and split knowledge. do you have a rotation schedule and KMS key hierarchies documented?
[05:36] Liam: yes, rotation policies are documented in our security whitepaper. for customer-managed keys, rotation is your responsibility; we recommend a yearly rotation and support automated rotation with minimal downtime. Redundancy-wise we support key hierarchies (data key wrapped by KMS).
[05:50] Sora: great.
[05:51] Maya: let's talk timeline: you mentioned Q3 requirement — is that end of September or earlier?
[05:56] Miguel: end of September, but our internal review needs to be complete mid-August to allow remediation time.
[06:03] Maya: ok so realistic timeline: 1) share redacted SOC2 and control matrix (this week), 2) configure SSO and onboard GRC users (2-3 weeks), 3) fill gaps and collect customer-specific evidence (by mid-August), 4) final audit readiness review in early September. does that align?
[06:18] Priya: yes, that seems right.
[06:19] Liam: technical deep dive — for KMS we should probably do a 30 minute session next week. we can go through kms key policies, encryption flow, and the minimal work to enable BYOK.
[06:30] Sora: sounds good.
[06:31] Maya: question from my side — do you have any regulatory data residency constraints beyond Japan? e.g., some of your partners have EU requirements.
[06:38] Priya: we may need eu-west retention for EU customers, yes. in terms of the trust center, we need the ability to segregate evidence by region or control set.
[06:46] Liam: we support partitioning and policy-based access — you can tag artifacts by region and restrict access by group. that will show up in the control matrix as well.
[06:54] Miguel: audit logs: are they tamper-evident? we need assurance that old logs can't be changed.
[06:59] Liam: logs are write-once for a defined window and we support immutability via object lock in S3-compatible storage; we also offer a cryptographic hash chain on critical events for extra assurance.
[07:12] Sora: ok that's reassuring.
[07:14] Miguel: any known gaps we should be aware of when moving forward?
[07:17] Liam: from platform side, the main items that often surface are: 1) customers not yet set up with SSO/group mapping, 2) missing linkage from deployment tickets to artifacts (so change control evidence is thin), and 3) if you opt for BYOK there are policy nuances to get right for rotation/backup.
[07:33] Maya: yep and on the admin side, sometimes teams need a short training on Trust Center workflows — how to tag evidence and set up retention policies. we can run a 45 minute workshop for your GRC and devops folks.
[07:43] Priya: can you run that in JP time? our GRC folks are in Kyoto office.
[07:47] Maya: yes, we can schedule regional sessions.
[07:49] Miguel: about evidence hand-off — we would prefer an automated pipeline. is there a recommended approach?
[07:54] Liam: best practice is to use our API to push CI/CD artifacts post-deploy. you can add a step that zips logs, attaches ticket metadata, and posts to the trust center. we have an example script in the KB.
[08:05] Sora: can you show the KB link?
[08:07] Maya: i'll include it in the follow-up; it's the 'evidence-onboarding' doc in the trust center docs. link: https://redwood.example.com/trustcenter/docs/evidence-onboarding (shared)
[08:18] Priya: thanks.
[08:20] Liam: small note — sometimes customers mention competitors like Megacloud AI who surface a similar control portal. difference is our crosswalk and model-level traceability; but i know feature parity conversations come up.
[08:33] Miguel: yeah we evaluated them briefly. one thing — they have a different model for KMS.
[08:36] Maya: ok, quick admin items: we'll need an NDA for external auditor invites, so if you want us to invite your external firm we can hold off until we have that. otherwise we can set up internal auditor roles first.
[08:49] Priya: we'll upload NDA to the trust center by monday.
[08:52] Maya: perfect. i'll send the redacted SOC2 and initial controls matrix after this call.
[08:57] Sora: on the control matrix, can you map our internal control ids? we use the format KB-xxx.
[09:02] Liam: yes just include a mapping file and we'll add a custom column in the matrix for your IDs.
[09:08] Miguel: one more thought — incident response evidence. auditors want to see post-incident review writeups and timelines. is there a template?
[09:15] Liam: we have an IR artifact template in the KB. we also keep incident timeline exports and retention tied to notifications in the trust center. i'll share that.
[09:24] Maya: ok let's recap next steps before we end.
[09:27] Maya: items for us: share redacted SOC 2 and controls matrix, invite for SSO setup, KB links for KMS and evidence onboarding, schedule KMS deep dive with liam.
[09:37] Sora: items for Kyoto: upload NDA, provide contact for GRC (miguel?), confirm region choices for retention, identify evidence owners.
[09:45] Miguel: yes i'll be the GRC contact and i'll circulate list of evidence owners by next tuesday.
[09:50] Priya: i'll share the product architecture doc with region mapping.
[09:53] Maya: awesome. any final questions?
[09:55] Sora: none here, thanks everyone.
[09:57] Maya: thanks all — we'll follow up with links and the invite. talk soon.
[10:01] (call ends)
